discovery: Proposal and realisation of electron-spin qubits in semiconductor quantum dots

nominees.name: Lieven M. K. Vandersypen
nominees.affiliation: QuTech and Delft University of Technology, Netherlands

nominees.name: Seigo Tarucha
nominees.affiliation: RIKEN Center for Emergent Matter Science, Japan

subfield: Condensed matter physics / semiconductor quantum information
motivation: In 1998 Daniel Loss, with DiVincenzo, showed that the spin of a single electron confined in a semiconductor quantum dot could serve as a qubit, with gates driven by electrically controlled exchange. This proposal set the agenda for a field. Seigo Tarucha built the few-electron quantum dots on which it rests, through his pioneering atom-like shell-filling experiments, and later achieved fast, high-fidelity electrical spin control using micromagnets. Lieven Vandersypen and co-workers achieved single-shot readout of an individual electron spin and coherent control of single spins, and then high-fidelity two-qubit gates and multi-qubit processors in silicon. Together these advances proved that quantum coherence of one electron spin can be created, controlled and measured in the same semiconductor platform that underpins modern electronics. The resulting physics is precise and reproducible, and it now supports scalable, industrially fabricated qubits.
